A poll taken after the debate gave Voss 46 percent and Rhee 44 percent, within the margin of error of 3 points, with 10 percent undecided. Norvia has 11 million voters and has been governed by a centre-left coalition since 2019. The debate lasted 90 minutes and was moderated by two journalists. Two other candidates, from the Green party and a small conservative movement, were not invited because their polling is below 5 percent.

In 1928 Alexander Fleming noticed that a mould had killed bacteria on one of his culture dishes at St Mary's Hospital in London. He identified the mould as Penicillium and named the active substance penicillin, but he struggled to purify it. It was not until 1940 that Howard Florey and Ernst Chain, working at Oxford, turned it into a usable drug. Mass production during the Second World War saved thousands of soldiers from infected wounds. Fleming was a Scottish bacteriologist who had earlier discovered lysozyme, an enzyme in tears and saliva. He shared the 1945 Nobel Prize with Florey and Chain. Early penicillin was so scarce that doctors sometimes recovered it from patients' urine so that it could be used again.
